entrypoints.summary: A supplied containerd gRPC configuration controls the Unix-socket address and uid/gid passed to local-listener setup; the report states that configuration-write ability is a necessary, potentially low-privileged precondition.

affected_components.role: GetLocalListener derives the socket parent and calls mkdirAs; mkdirAs conditionally creates it and changes ownership to its uid/gid arguments.

code_slices.fixed: No implementation patch is present; the report recommends inheriting ownership from the directory used to create the new directory.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The created directory is the parent of the configured Unix-domain socket path.
code_slices.vulnerable: GetLocalListener(path, uid, gid) calls mkdirAs(filepath.Dir(path), uid, gid); mkdirAs performs os.Mkdir(path, 0770) followed by os.Chown(path, uid, gid) when the path does not exist.

capabilities.concept: attacker-selected ownership of a newly created socket-parent directory

impacts.concept: persistent attacker-owned directory under a sensitive filesystem hierarchy

mitigations.concept: inherit ownership from the parent directory for new socket-parent directories

impact.affected_asset: Filesystem directory hierarchy, including the demonstrated /etc/cron.d/new_dir location.
impact.attacker_capability: An actor able to provide the relevant configuration to a privileged containerd instance can select the socket-parent path and its uid/gid when the parent directory is absent.
impact.security_effect: Conditional creation of a persistent attacker-owned directory at a configuration-selected location under a sensitive filesystem hierarchy.

causal_trace.summary: A malicious gRPC configuration supplies an address beneath a chosen filesystem hierarchy and uid/gid values.

GetLocalListener derives the socket address's parent directory and passes that path plus the supplied uid/gid to mkdirAs, allowing privileged socket setup to use configuration-selected ownership for a new parent directory.
If the parent does not exist, mkdirAs calls os.Mkdir(path, 0770) and then os.Chown(path, uid, gid).
The supplied PoC creates /etc/cron.d/new_dir and assigns uid/gid 1000, producing a persistent directory under a sensitive hierarchy with non-root ownership.

failure.operation: os.Chown(path, uid, gid) after creation of the socket parent directory

primary_invariant.statement: When privileged listener setup creates a missing socket-parent directory, its ownership should follow the parent hierarchy rather than configuration-provided uid/gid values.
primary_invariant.violated_because: mkdirAs creates the selected parent path and explicitly changes its owner and group to the uid/gid supplied to GetLocalListener.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report embeds both the relevant code excerpt and a configuration PoC, and reports the resulting directory and ownership. The bundle contains no immutable upstream file revision, fix commit, regression test, or execution harness. Configuration-write/reload access is a deployment-specific precondition. The report did not demonstrate cron execution: cron rejected the non-root-owned directory on its test system; possible trust by other applications is conditional.

remediation.invariant_restored: A newly created socket-parent directory inherits the owner of the directory used to create it, rather than honoring supplied uid/gid values.
mitigation_classes: inherit parent-directory ownership during privileged directory creation

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The actor must be able to supply the relevant gRPC configuration to a privileged containerd process, select an address whose parent is absent, and provide uid/gid values.
data_structure_invariants: A new socket-parent directory should preserve ownership expectations of its containing hierarchy.
Ownership of a privileged daemon-created directory should not be selected by gRPC configuration uid/gid.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The PoC uses uid 1000 and gid 1000; the report says owner and group ID can be set arbitrarily.
numeric_domains.name: uid/gid

state_context.state_machine: A configured listener path is processed; if its parent does not exist, mkdirAs creates it and assigns the supplied uid/gid before Unix-socket creation proceeds.
